questions.q: Why isn't a rule that only watches CommonSecurityLog enough on its own?
options: CommonSecurityLog doesn't exist in Sentinel
An external address allowed through the firewall to an admin port is also true for every legitimate vendor session, including Meridian's
Firewall logs can't be queried with KQL
It only works for Windows, not Linux
questions.explain: Watching the firewall alone can't separate a routine vendor session from something worth a human's attention -- both look the same from that one source.

questions.q: What is this analytics rule named, and what does it watch?
options: Brute-Force Logon Detector; watches only SigninLogs
External RDP Allow + Entra Sign-In Correlation; watches CommonSecurityLog for RDP allows and SigninLogs for sign-ins from the same address
Linux Syslog Anomaly Rule; watches only Syslog
CEF Health Check; watches connector status only
questions.explain: The rule joins firewall allow events reaching the RDP port against Entra ID sign-ins from the same source address.

questions.q: In the join `RdpAllows | join kind=inner EntraSignIns on $left.SourceIP == $right.IPAddress`, what does `$left` refer to?
options: EntraSignIns
RdpAllows, the table before the join
Neither table
The Sentinel workspace itself
questions.explain: $left refers to the table before `join` -- here, RdpAllows -- and $right refers to the table inside the parentheses, EntraSignIns.

questions.q: What does the `where SignInTime > FirewallTime and SignInTime < FirewallTime + 15m` clause enforce?
options: Nothing -- it's optional
That the sign-in landed after the firewall allow and within 15 minutes of it, not just sometime in the same hour
That the sign-in happened before the firewall allow
That the two events happened on different days
questions.explain: This keeps the match tight: a sign-in shortly after the firewall allow, from the same address -- a narrower, more specific pattern than either event alone.

questions.q: Why does this one rule serve both Owen and Renee at the same time?
options: It doesn't -- it only serves Owen
It gives Owen real cross-source visibility and gives Renee a documented detection built for a specific, named threat scenario
It replaces the need for an incident-response runbook entirely
It only matters for compliance, not operations
questions.explain: The rule is both the operational visibility Owen wants and the auditable, use-case-justified detection Renee wants.
